newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks end mixed, IBB ends 18-day rally.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks end mixed, IBB ends 18-day rally.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed after profit-taking put an end to an impressive 18-day rally in Bogota where the price index has gained more than 25 percent in peso terms since the start of the year.

Bogota's IBB index ended down 0.25 percent at 1,038.52 on a trading volume of 7.7 billion pesos. The IBOMED general price index in Medellin closed up 1.28 percent, however, ending at 16,419.70, it highest level since mid-1995.
Brokers said the profit-taking that snapped the rally in Bogota was a normal reaction to the sharp run-up in valuations and did not necessarily mean the market's glory days were over.
"It was a normal price correction after the quick gains," one broker said of the year's first drop in Bogota. "The market grew a lot, and speculators took advantage of that to sell," he said.
He and others said Colombian stocks were still widely seen as undervalued, however, and that overall demand was expected to continue in the days and weeks ahead.

Losers in Bogota were led by insurance giant Suramericana de Seguros, which fell 9.88 percent to close at 21,510 pesos per share. Gainers included cement makers Cementos Caribe, which ended up 8.23 percent at 5,520 pesos a share, and Cemento Argos, which rose 1.44 percent to close at 7,000 pesos per share.

The day's biggest winner by far was Corporacion Financiera Nacional y Suramericana, an investment banking and credit firm belonging to the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate. It jumped 27.71 percent in Medellin to close at 2,300 pesos per share. Brokers said the firm's highly liquid stock had been in short supply until Wednesday during the rally that has seen Medellin's price index gain 20.77 percent this year.
Brokers ruled out any link between the drop in Bogota and the economic emergency declared by the central government Monday to slash its growing fiscal deficit.
